executive_summary.headline: Enterprise platforms are packaging faster models with governance controls.
executive_summary.body: This week’s clearest launches pair model or runtime improvements with region, spend, identity, and observability controls that make evaluation more actionable.

executive_summary.headline: The near-term test is workflow economics, not headline capability.
executive_summary.body: Ultrafast inference, persistent sessions, and broader model catalogs are useful only when task cost, latency, residency, and rollback are measured together.

top_picks.title: OpenAI previews Ultrafast GPT-5.6 Sol service tier
top_picks.author: OpenAI
top_picks.summary: The official announcement describes a limited preview of GPT-5.6 Sol on Cerebras hardware at up to 14 times the standard processing speed, aimed at latency-sensitive workflows.
top_picks.competitive_context: The strategic question is whether lower latency changes the feasible workflow while preserving model, data, and budget controls.
top_picks.pricing: Limited preview; public pricing not stated in the announcement.
key_takeaways: Benchmark time to useful result and tool-call count.
Treat faster loops as a spend-control issue.
Confirm capacity and data handling before a pilot.

top_picks.title: Bedrock adds GPT-5.6 models and cross-Region inference
top_picks.author: Amazon Web Services
top_picks.summary: The official launch adds GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna through Responses, Converse, and Chat Completions APIs, with global and geography-scoped cross-Region inference.
top_picks.competitive_context: The geographic routing options make throughput and residency part of the same architecture decision.
top_picks.pricing: Pricing varies by model and Bedrock terms; validate current account pricing.
key_takeaways: Geo routing can raise capacity without changing application code.
Residency claims need an explicit route test.

top_picks.title: Google expands Antigravity for enterprise customers
top_picks.author: Google Cloud
top_picks.summary: The announcement adds Antigravity to eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions with administrative, spend, security, observability, and usage controls.
top_picks.competitive_context: Bundling developer agents with enterprise administration raises the importance of tenant policy and usage telemetry.
top_picks.pricing: Included for eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions; exact license terms depend on plan.
key_takeaways: Admin and spend controls are part of the product surface.
Observability must follow the agent into developer workflows.

top_picks.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash reaches general availability
top_picks.author: Google Cloud
top_picks.summary: Release notes list Gemini 3.7 Flash as GA for production use, with agentic video processing enabled by default.
top_picks.competitive_context: A production-ready workhorse model can shift the portfolio toward routing by task cost and latency.
top_picks.pricing: See current Google Cloud model pricing.
key_takeaways: Video processing expands multimodal workflow scope.
Task routing still needs independent evaluation.

top_picks.title: Bedrock AgentCore adds persistent runtime instances
top_picks.author: Amazon Web Services
top_picks.summary: The AWS roundup describes managed EC2-backed runtime instances for production agents, multi-agent collaboration, GPU support, and sessions lasting up to 14 days.
top_picks.competitive_context: Long-lived managed sessions increase capability and the need for lifecycle, budget, and data-retention controls.
top_picks.pricing: See current Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing.
key_takeaways: Session duration is an architecture choice.
Persistent state needs retention and deletion policy.
GPU-backed runtimes increase cost visibility requirements.
